Uthman told Ibn az-Zubair he would not move anything of the Quran from its place, keeping the widows' verse said to be abrogated.
The Prophet said we have more right to doubt than Abraham, who asked Allah to show him how He gives life to the dead so his faith would be stronger.
Ibn Abbas called the verse of the garden a parable for deeds; Umar explained it as a rich man whose good deeds are lost when Satan leads him into sin.
The Prophet said the poor person is not the one a date or a morsel will satisfy, but the one who does not beg from people or show his poverty.
When the verses of Al-Baqara on usury were revealed the Prophet recited them and prohibited trade in alcohol; Ibn Abbas said the usury verse was the last revealed.
Ibn Umar said the verse 'whether you show what is in your minds or conceal it' was abrogated by the verse following it.
The Prophet recited the verse on the Book's clear and unclear verses and warned against those who follow the unclear ones, saying Allah named them as deviating.
Satan touches every newborn child, who cries out at his touch, except Mary and her son.
A false oath taken to seize a Muslim's property brings Allah's anger; the verse is linked to Al-Ash'ath's well and a trader's false oath, and the defendant takes the oath.
Heraclius of Byzantium questioned Abu Sufyan about the Prophet, said the answers marked a true prophet, and read the letter calling him to Islam and to a common word.
When the verse on spending what you love was revealed, Abu Talha gave his beloved Bairuha garden in Allah's Cause, and on the Prophet's advice divided it among his relatives.
Jews brought a man and woman who had committed illegal intercourse; when Abdullah bin Salam exposed the stoning verse hidden in the Torah, the Prophet ordered them stoned.
Abu Huraira explained 'the best of peoples' as the best for people, who bring others with chains on their necks until they embrace Islam.
Jabir said the verse about two parties about to lose heart, with Allah their Protector, concerned Banu Haritha and Banu Salama, and they were glad it was revealed.
After bowing in prayer the Prophet cursed certain people and tribes and prayed for named men to be saved, until the verse 'Not for you is the decision' came.
At Uhud the infantry under Abdullah bin Jubair returned defeated, leaving twelve men with the Prophet, and slumber overtook Abu Talha till his sword kept falling.
'Allah is sufficient for us and the best Disposer of affairs' was said by Abraham when thrown into the fire, and by Muhammad when warned of a great army.
Wealth whose zakat is unpaid will become a bald poisonous snake on the Day of Resurrection, coiling round its owner's neck and biting his cheeks.
Abdullah bin Ubai rebuffed the Prophet's preaching; the Prophet excused him, for Muslims were then ordered to forgive the pagans and People of the Scripture until fighting was permitted.
Some hypocrites stayed behind from the Prophet's campaigns, then made false excuses and oaths, wanting praise for what they had not done, so the verse about them was revealed.
Ibn Abbas told Marwan the verse on loving praise for what one has not done concerned Jews who hid the truth from the Prophet and wanted praise for answering.
Staying with his aunt Maimuna, Ibn Abbas saw the Prophet wake at night, recite the last ten verses of Al Imran and pray two by two, ending with witr.
Guardians were forbidden to marry orphan girls for their wealth or beauty without a fair dowry, and a poor guardian may take a reasonable wage from the orphan's property.
The inheritance verses cover relatives present at the division, the shares of children, parents and spouses, the ban on inheriting women against their will, and ending inheritance by brotherhood.
Believers will see Allah on the Day of Resurrection as clearly as the sun and full moon, after each nation that worshipped other than Allah falls into Hell.
Ibn Masud recited An-Nisa to the Prophet, who liked hearing the Quran from others; at the verse on a witness from each nation he stopped him, eyes overflowing with tears.
When Asma's necklace was lost and the men searching for it prayed without ablution for lack of water, Allah revealed the verse of tayammum.
Ibn Abbas said the verse on obeying Allah, the Apostle and those in authority was revealed about Abdullah bin Hudhafa when the Prophet made him commander of a detachment.
When an Ansari disputing water claimed the Prophet favoured his cousin Az-Zubair, the Prophet gave Az-Zubair his full right; Az-Zubair linked the verse on making the Prophet judge.
Every sick prophet is offered this world or the Hereafter; in his last illness the Prophet recited the verse on those Allah blessed, and Aisha knew he was offered it.
Reciting the verse excepting weak men, women and children, Ibn Abbas said he and his mother were among the weak Muslims at Mecca whom Allah excused.
When some companions turned back from Uhud, Muslims split over whether to kill them; the verse on dividing over the hypocrites came, and the Prophet said Medina expels impurities.
Ibn Abbas said the verse giving Hell to whoever kills a believer intentionally was never abrogated; another verse came after Muslims killed a man who greeted them with peace.
When the blind Ibn Umm Maktum heard the verse ranking strivers above those who sit at home, the exception for the disabled came; Ibn Abbas applied it to Badr.
Ikrima forbade joining an army against Sham, citing Muslims killed while swelling the pagans' numbers against the Prophet; Ibn Abbas said his mother was among the excused weak.
In the Isha prayer the Prophet asked Allah to save Aiyash, Salama, Al-Walid and the weak believers, and to punish the tribe of Mudar with years of famine.
Ibn Abbas said the verse allowing for the inconvenience of rain or illness was revealed concerning Abdur-Rahman bin Auf, who was wounded.
Aisha said the verse on instructions about women concerns a guardian who keeps an orphan girl sharing his property from marrying, neither marrying her himself nor letting another.
Aisha said the verse on a wife fearing cruelty or desertion concerns a husband who wants to divorce her, while she tells him she frees him as regards herself.
Hudhaifa said people better than those present had become hypocrites, and then repented and Allah forgave them.
